title: T1001 — Data Obfuscation
subtitle: Watch one obfuscated C2 session unfold, and watch the defenders catch it with metadata instead of content.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: A strange first hello
steps.caption: The infected PC opens a session whose first bytes match no known protocol, because key fields are scrambled with a simple XOR cipher.
steps.defender: look at the connection shape, not the content - a first packet that fits no known protocol is a lead.

steps.caption: The C2 server answers like an ordinary web page, but the Set-Cookie header carries a blob of more than 500 bytes - the next command.
steps.defender: a Set-Cookie value far longer than normal on this host deserves a look.

steps.title: Results go home, scrambled
steps.caption: The result is uploaded in a POST body encrypted with XOR and RC4, repeating on a steady 60-second beat.
steps.defender: a steady cadence plus opaque bodies is the pattern to catch.

steps.defender: content is blind, metadata is not - a 40-minute session with regular small uploads stands out.
